points.problem: Global reduced-motion support existed but had no automated regression guard, allowing accessibility behavior to be silently removed or weakened.
points.implementation: lint:ux-regressions now validates presence of prefers-reduced-motion and the required scroll, animation, loop and transition suppression contracts.
points.evidence: Git fallback commit 2e0db0c3cba8b5276c0897c3a7aab46fa6b75c02 on main. VPS offline, so command/runtime execution is pending.

points.problem: Production smoke checked root and critical assets but could silently pass after loss of baseline browser security headers.
points.implementation: Runtime smoke now fails on missing/invalid X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Content-Security-Policy and, for HTTPS, Strict-Transport-Security.
points.evidence: Git fallback commit 709e04a1cd1e401fca1a2b3f8812dfa4ac4b0d36 on main. VPS offline, so runtime execution is pending.

points.problem: Shared main enforced per-chunk and total JavaScript budgets but did not independently cap JavaScript loaded by build/index.html at bootstrap, allowing initial-load regressions to hide inside the larger total budget.
points.implementation: perf:budget now discovers local script assets referenced by build/index.html, fails closed if none/missing, enforces a 250 KiB gzip initial-JS ceiling, and reports bootstrap asset count, size and budget percentage without lowering existing limits.
points.evidence: Git fallback commit b8985df748cefe106d080271a970ff116c616f06 on main. VPS offline; command/build execution pending.
points.next: When VPS returns, sync main, run production build and npm run perf:budget; compare initial JS with prior 121 KiB baseline and investigate any material increase.

points.problem: A visible global :focus-visible keyboard treatment existed but had no automated regression contract, so it could be silently removed, made transparent or collapsed to zero width/offset.
points.implementation: lint:ux-regressions now fails closed when the global :focus-visible rule is missing or its outline/offset is non-visible, while preserving the existing reduced-motion and forbidden-pattern checks.
points.evidence: Git fallback commit 1eb05b1e776fe3b31d7c2469ada083ce53cc3fdf on main. Current global.css has 2px solid var(--cut-primary) outline with 3px offset. VPS offline; command/browser execution pending.
points.next: When VPS returns, sync main, run npm run lint:ux-regressions and keyboard-tab smoke on public event/production/navigation flows.

points.problem: New JSX images could be introduced without alt semantics and the existing architecture guard would not detect the accessibility regression.
points.implementation: lint:ux-regressions now inspects added production source lines and fails when a newly added lacks an explicit alt attribute, while allowing alt="" for decorative imagery.
points.evidence: Git fallback commit 329ed7abde4f4ee874ffb60842476ae34d2e7ebd on main. GitHub exposes no checks for the commit yet; VPS is offline so command execution is pending.
points.next: When VPS returns, sync main and run npm run lint:ux-regressions; then continue browser-level accessibility smoke on public views.
